==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɜːli/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-early.ogg}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɝli/|/ɚ̞li/|a=GA,CA}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-early.ogg}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɜː(ɹ)li|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|ear|ly}}
* {{homophones|en|Earley}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymid|en|adjective}}
From {{inh|en|enm|erly}}, {{m|enm|erlich}}, {{m|enm|earlich}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ǣrlīċ|t=early|pos=adjective}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|ere|ly|id2=adjectival}}.

====Adjective====
{{en-adj|er}}

# At a [[time]] in [[advance]] of the usual or expected event.
#: {{ux|en|at eleven, we went for an '''early''' lunch;  she began reading at an '''early''' age;  his mother suffered an '''early''' death}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-29|volume=407|issue=8842|page=28
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/asia/21580209-natural-disaster-aggravated-poor-response-high-and-wet High and wet]
|passage=Floods in northern India, mostly in the small state of Uttarakhand, have wrought disaster on an enormous scale. The '''early''', intense onset of the monsoon on June 14th swelled rivers, washing away roads, bridges, hotels and even whole villages. Rock-filled torrents smashed vehicles and homes, burying victims under rubble and sludge.}}
# [[arrive|Arriving]] a time [[before]] expected; sooner than [[on time]].
#: {{ux|en|You're '''early''' today! I don't usually see you before nine o'clock.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''early''' guests sipped their punch and avoided each other's eyes.}}
# [[after|After]] but [[close to]] the [[start]] of a period of time.
#: {{ux|en|The play "Two Gentlemen of Verona" is one of Shakespeare's '''early''' works.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Early''' results showed their winning 245 out of 300 seats in parliament. The main opponent locked up only 31 seats.}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=1|passage='Twas '''early''' June, the new grass was flourishing everywheres, the posies in the yard—peonies and such—in full bloom, the sun was shining, and the water of the bay was blue, with light green streaks where the shoal showed.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-07-20|volume=408|issue=8845
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/http://www.economist.com/news/business/21582001-army-new-online-courses-scaring-wits-out-traditional-universities-can-they The attack of the MOOCs]
|passage=Dotcom mania was slow in coming to higher education, but now it has the venerable industry firmly in its grip. Since the launch '''early''' last year of Udacity and Coursera, two Silicon Valley start-ups offering free education through MOOCs, massive open online courses, the ivory towers of academia have been shaken to their foundations.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Corinna da Fonseca-Wollheim|title=Ticktock as Taskmaster: A Show About Metronomes and Musical Time|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/30/arts/music/ticktock-as-taskmaster-a-show-about-metronomes-and-musical-time.html|date=2017-06-30|passage=It’s one of the '''earliest''' pieces in the comprehensive collection of metronomes by the British instrument dealer Tony Bingham, which forms the bulk of the Basel exhibition.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230517174410/http://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/30/arts/music/ticktock-as-taskmaster-a-show-about-metronomes-and-musical-time.html|archivedate=17 May 2023}}
# In the starting hours of the day.
#: {{ux|en|It's too '''early''' for this sort of thing. I'm not awake yet.}}
# Having begun to [[occur]]; in its early stages.
#: {{ux|en|'''early''' cancer}}
#: {{ux|en|harvesting '''early''' peaches}}
# {{lb|en|astronomy}} Of a star or class of stars, hotter than the sun.
#: {{antonyms|en|late}}

=====Synonyms=====
* {{qualifier|at a time in advance of the usual}}: [[premature]]
* {{qualifier|near but after the start}}: [[first]]
* {{qualifier|ripening before other}}: [[new]]

=====Antonyms=====
* {{qualifier|at a time in advance of the usual}}: [[late]]
* {{qualifier|illness: having begun to occur}}: [[terminal]]

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|informal}} A [[shift]] {{gl|scheduled work period}} that takes place early in the day.

=====Antonyms=====
* {{l|en|late}}

===Etymology 2===
{{etymon|en|id=adverb|:inh|enm:erly<id:adverb>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|erly}}, {{m|enm|orely}}, {{m|enm|arely}}, {{m|enm|erliche}}, {{m|enm|arliche}}, from {{inh|en|ang|ǣrlīċe}}, {{m|ang|ārlīċe|t=early; early in the morning|pos=adverb}}, equivalent to {{suf|en|ere|ly|id2=adverbial}}. Cognate with {{cog|non|árliga}}, {{m|non|árla}} ( > {{cog|da|årle}}, {{cog|sv|arla}}, {{cog|no|årle}}, {{cog|fo|árla}}).

====Adverb====
{{en-adv|er}}

# At a time [[before]] expected; sooner than [[usual]].
#: {{ux|en|We finished the project an hour sooner than scheduled, so we left '''early'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|I had children too '''early''' (in life), so my first baby arrived '''early'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|page=46|passage=No matter how '''early''' I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or otherwise his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly join me if I would kindly wait.}}
# {{U|soon}}; in good time; [[seasonably]].
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Proverbs|8|17|page=729|column=1|passage=[T]thoſe that ſeeke me '''early''', ſhall find me.}}
#* {{RQ:Tennyson Poems 1833|poem=The May Queen|page=90|stanza=I|passage=You must wake and call me '''early''', call me '''early''', mother dear; / Tomorrow 'ill be the happiest time of all the blythe Newyear; {{...}}}}

=====Synonyms=====
* {{l|en|prematurely}}

=====Antonyms=====
* {{l|en|late}}, {{l|en|tardily}}

=====Derived terms=====
* {{l|en|bright and early}}
* {{l|en|Christmas come early}}
